# Implementation Plan — Adaptive Delivery Routing System

A live, self-adjusting delivery routing platform. It plans routes once, then **re-optimizes only the affected part** of the plan as real-world events hit — new orders, breakdowns, traffic, cancellations, time-window changes, priority orders — without discarding deliveries already completed or in progress.

> Build order: **frontend first (on mock data), backend second**, then wire them together. This lets us demo a believable UI early and push visible progress often.

 *

## 0\. Assumptions & Tech Stack

Chosen defaults (swap if you prefer — noted so you can veto early):

| Layer | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frontend | Next.js 14 (App Router) + TypeScript | Routing, SEO, one framework end-to-end |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui | Quick, clean, consistent |
| Map | Leaflet via `react-leaflet` + OpenStreetMap tiles | Free, no API key |
| State | Zustand | Minimal boilerplate, good for live state |
| Charts | Recharts | Before/After dashboards |
| Live link | [Socket.IO](http://Socket.IO) client | Push position + re-opt updates |
| Backend | Python 3.11 + FastAPI + Uvicorn | OR-Tools is Python-native |
| Optimizer | Google OR-Tools (`ortools`) routing | Required by spec |
| Realtime | `python-socketio` (ASGI) | Broadcast sim ticks + events |
| Distances | OSRM demo / OpenRouteService, haversine×1.3 fallback | Real road times, offline-safe |
| Store | In-memory state + optional SQLite (SQLModel) | Simulation is ephemeral |

**Key design principle:** the backend holds the *source of truth* for world state (vehicle live positions, delivery status, current plan). The frontend renders it. The optimizer is a pure function `(world_state, locks) -> plan`.

 *

## 1\. The Core Idea — Dynamic Re-Optimization (read this first)

This is the part that wins or loses the project, so the whole architecture is built around it.

**Naive approach (what we avoid):** on every event, throw away the plan and re-solve the full VRP from scratch. Slow, and it reshuffles routes drivers are already driving — unusable in the real world.

**Our approach — freeze + warm-start + partial re-solve:**

1. Freeze the past. Deliveries already COMPLETED are removed from the model entirely. They cost nothing and cannot move.
2. Respect commitment. A stop that is IN_PROGRESS (driver already departed toward it) is locked as that vehicle’s mandatory next visit — the solver may not reassign or reorder it.
3. Move the start. Each vehicle re-enters the model at its current live position (interpolated along its polyline), not the depot.
4. Re-solve only the tail. Only unvisited stops + newly affected orders form the free pool the solver rearranges.
5. Warm-start. The previous routes (minus completed) are fed to OR-Tools as the initial solution. With a short time limit (2–5s), the solver improves from the existing plan instead of starting from zero — this literally implements “without throwing away all previous work.”
6. Allow drops. Orders are added with a priority-scaled penalty (disjunction), so an over-constrained situation (e.g. breakdown) drops the lowest-priority orders rather than returning “infeasible.”

The example from the brief — *2 of 5 delivered, then an event hits* — falls out naturally: those 2 are `COMPLETED` (dropped from the model), stop 3 may be locked if the driver is en route, and only stops 4–5 (+ any new orders) get re-optimized.

## 2\. Architecture & Data Flow

```scss
┌─────────────┐   REST (CRUD, trigger event)   ┌──────────────────────┐
│  React UI   │ ─────────────────────────────► │   FastAPI backend    │
│  (Leaflet)  │ ◄───────────── Socket.IO ────── │                      │
└─────────────┘   ticks, positions, new plans   │  ┌────────────────┐  │
                                                 │  │ World State    │  │
                                                 │  │ (vehicles,     │  │
                                                 │  │  orders, plan) │  │
                                                 │  └───────┬────────┘  │
                                                 │          │           │
                                                 │  ┌───────▼────────┐  │
                                                 │  │ Sim clock loop │  │
                                                 │  │ (asyncio tick) │  │
                                                 │  └───────┬────────┘  │
                                                 │  ┌───────▼────────┐  │
                                                 │  │ OR-Tools engine│  │
                                                 │  │ initial + re-  │  │
                                                 │  │ optimize       │  │
                                                 │  └────────────────┘  │
                                                 └──────────────────────┘
```

Flow: user triggers an event → backend mutates world state → re-optimization engine computes a new plan honoring locks → new plan + metrics broadcast over [Socket.IO](http://Socket.IO) → UI animates the change and updates the Before/After panel.

## 4\. Phase Plan

Each phase lists **goal → tasks → done-when**. Phases 0–3 are frontend, 4–6 backend, 7–8 integration & polish. Commit checkpoints (§9) are interleaved so we push every ~3h.

### Phase 0 — Scaffolding

**Goal:** empty but runnable frontend + backend shells.

*   Init `frontend/` (Next.js App Router, TS), Tailwind, shadcn, folder structure. Leaflet loads via dynamic import (`ssr: false`) since it needs `window`.
*   Init `backend/` (FastAPI hello-world, requirements, venv), health endpoint.
*   Root README with run instructions.
*   **Done when:** `npm run dev` shows a blank app; `uvicorn` returns `/health` 200.

### Phase 1 — Live Map (mock data)

**Goal:** the map that sells the demo, running purely on mock data.

*   Full-screen Leaflet map + app shell (map center, right sidebar, bottom bar).
*   Render layers from mock JSON: depot, vehicles (truck markers), delivery pins (colored by priority), route polylines per vehicle.
*   Vehicle marker popup: id, driver, load/capacity, status.
*   Legend + layer toggles.
*   **Done when:** map shows 3–5 vehicles with distinct colored routes and ~15 delivery pins from `mock/`.

### Phase 2 — Order & Vehicle Management (frontend)

**Goal:** create/edit the entities the optimizer will consume.

*   **Order form:** location (click-on-map or lat/lng/address), delivery window (start–end time), size/weight, priority (Low/Med/High/Critical).
*   **Order list/table:** status chip, priority, window, assigned vehicle.
*   **Vehicle panel:** location, capacity (weight + volume), current load, driver name, driver availability, shift start/end (working-hour limit).
*   All backed by the Zustand store (still mock; no server yet).
*   **Done when:** adding an order drops a pin on the map; editing a vehicle updates its popup.

### Phase 3 — Event Simulator + Before/After Dashboard (frontend)

**Goal:** the two headline panels, driven by mock/stub responses.

*   **Event Simulator panel** with a control for each case:
    
    1. Add new order
    2. Vehicle breakdown (pick vehicle)
    3. Traffic increase (pick area/road + severity)
    4. Order cancellation (pick order)
    5. Delivery time change (pick order + new window)
    6. Delivery address change (pick order + new location)
    7. Priority order appears (add order flagged Critical)
    
*   **Before/After panel** (Recharts): total distance, total delivery time, late deliveries, # route changes, vehicle utilization %, re-optimization time (ms). Two-column compare + delta badges.
*   Simulation transport: Play/Pause/speed, sim clock display.
*   **Done when:** clicking an event visibly mutates the mock plan and the Before/After panel animates deltas.

> End of frontend-first block. The app looks complete on mock data. Everything after this replaces mocks with a real backend.

### Phase 4 — Backend Data Models & API

**Goal:** real world-state + CRUD, no optimization yet.

*   Pydantic/SQLModel schemas (see §5).
*   In-memory `WorldState` store (vehicles, orders, plan, sim\_time).
*   REST: CRUD orders, CRUD vehicles, `GET /state`, seed/reset endpoints.
*   Distance matrix service: OSRM/ORS call with haversine×1.3 fallback + in-memory cache.
*   **Done when:** frontend `mock/` is swapped for real `GET /state`; CRUD round-trips.

### Phase 5 — Initial Route Optimizer (OR-Tools)

**Goal:** assign all orders to vehicles and produce efficient routes.

*   Build OR-Tools routing model with constraints (see §7): capacity, time windows, working hours, travel time, priority.
*   Priority-scaled disjunction penalties so low-value orders can drop when infeasible.
*   `POST /optimize` → returns plan (per-vehicle ordered stop list, ETAs, distance).
*   Persist plan into `WorldState`; broadcast over socket.
*   **Done when:** a seeded scenario returns a valid multi-vehicle plan the map can draw.

### Phase 6 — Dynamic Re-Optimization Engine ⭐ (most important)

**Goal:** the freeze + warm-start + partial re-solve loop from §1.

*   Delivery status tracking: `PENDING → ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED`.
*   Lock logic: drop `COMPLETED`; pin `IN_PROGRESS` as mandatory first visit; start each vehicle at its live position.
*   Warm-start: feed previous routes as initial solution (`ReadAssignmentFromRoutes`), short time limit.
*   Six event handlers (see §6) each mutate state then call `reoptimize(locks)`.
*   Emit a **diff**: which vehicles/orders changed, so the UI highlights only those and the metric “# route changes” is real.
*   **Done when:** the “2 of 5 delivered, event after stop 2” scenario re-optimizes stops 4–5 only, leaving 1–3 untouched, in < 5s.

### Phase 7 — Integration: Simulation Clock & Live Sync

**Goal:** make “drivers already departed” real.

*   `asyncio` tick loop advances `sim_time`; vehicles interpolate along polylines; on stop arrival mark delivered; broadcast positions.
*   [Socket.IO](http://Socket.IO) events: `state:update`, `vehicle:move`, `plan:changed`, `event:applied`.
*   Frontend consumes sockets; remove remaining mock paths; Play/Pause/speed control the backend clock.
*   **Done when:** pressing Play animates trucks; triggering an event mid-drive re-routes only remaining work live.

### Phase 8 — Metrics, Before/After, Polish, Demo

**Goal:** trustworthy numbers + a clean demo.

*   `metrics.py` computes all six KPIs from a plan; snapshot before/after each re-opt.
*   Wire real deltas into the Before/After panel; record re-optimization wall-clock.
*   Edge cases: all-drop, breakdown with no spare capacity, window already missed.
*   Seed 2–3 scripted demo scenarios; write demo runbook (§10).
*   **Done when:** full demo runs start-to-finish without manual data fixing.

## 5\. Data Models (core fields)

```python
Depot        { id, location(lat,lng) }

Order        { id, location, address,
               window_start, window_end,        # delivery time window
               weight, volume,                  # package size
               priority: 1..4,                  # 4 = critical
               status: PENDING|ASSIGNED|IN_PROGRESS|COMPLETED|CANCELLED|DROPPED,
               assigned_vehicle, seq_index, eta }

Vehicle      { id, location(live), capacity_weight, capacity_volume,
               current_load, speed_kmh, status: ACTIVE|BROKEN|IDLE,
               driver, driver_available: bool,
               shift_start, shift_end }          # working-hour limit

RouteStop    { order_id, seq, arrival_eta, locked: bool }
Plan         { vehicle_id -> [RouteStop], generated_at, solve_ms }

Event        { type, payload, sim_time }
Metrics      { total_distance_km, total_time_min, late_deliveries,
               route_changes, utilization_pct, reopt_ms }
```

 *

## 6\. Event → Re-Optimization Mapping

Every handler does: **mutate state → compute locks → `reoptimize()` → diff → broadcast.**

| Event | State mutation | Locks / effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **New order** | insert `PENDING` order | insert into free pool; warm-start keeps others stable, solver slots it in |
| **Priority order** | insert order `priority=4` | high keep-penalty forces assignment; may bump a low-priority order to DROPPED |
| **Vehicle breakdown** | vehicle `BROKEN`, capacity→0 | its unvisited stops released to pool; completed stay; re-solve across remaining vehicles |
| **Traffic increase** | multiply durations on affected arcs/region ×severity | matrix update only; re-solve may resequence to dodge slow arcs |
| **Order cancellation** | order `CANCELLED` | remove from pool; freed slack lets solver tighten routes |
| **Delivery time change** | update `window_start/end` | if now infeasible on current vehicle, reassign; else resequence |
| **Delivery address change** | update `location`, refresh matrix rows | treat as move; re-solve affected vehicle(s) |

In every case: `COMPLETED` stops are gone from the model and `IN_PROGRESS` stops are pinned, so committed/finished work is never disturbed.

 *

## 7\. OR-Tools Design Deep-Dive

**Model:** `RoutingIndexManager` + `RoutingModel`. Nodes = depot + active orders. Vehicles start at their live position (add per-vehicle start nodes), end at depot or open-ended.

**Dimensions & constraints:**

*   **Capacity** — `AddDimensionWithVehicleCapacity` on weight (and a second dimension on volume). Vehicle start load = `current_load`.
*   **Time / travel** — `AddDimension` on travel duration (from the matrix). This carries ETAs.
*   **Delivery windows** — `time_dim.CumulVar(node).SetRange(window_start, window_end)` per order.
*   **Working hours** — bound each vehicle’s time cumul at its end node to `shift_end`; start at `max(sim_time, shift_start)`.
*   **Priority** — `AddDisjunction([node], penalty)` with `penalty = base × priority`. High penalty = “really try to serve”; unserved becomes `DROPPED`.
*   **Driver availability** — a vehicle with `driver_available=False` or `status=BROKEN` gets no free nodes (only its locked prefix, if any) or is excluded.

**Locking for re-optimization (the crux):**

*   `COMPLETED` orders: not added to the model at all.
*   `IN_PROGRESS` order for vehicle *v*: add it, then force it first + on *v* via `SetAllowedVehiclesForIndex([v], idx)` and a first-position constraint; or pass it inside *v*’s locked prefix in the initial routes.
*   **Warm start:** `initial = routing.ReadAssignmentFromRoutes(previous_routes_without_completed, True)`, then `SolveFromAssignmentWithParameters(initial, search_params)`.
*   `search_params.time_limit` = 2–5s; `first_solution_strategy = PATH_CHEAPEST_ARC` (only used if no warm start); `local_search_metaheuristic = GUIDED_LOCAL_SEARCH`.

**Why this is fast & stable:** the search begins *at* the current plan and is time-boxed, so it returns a plan close to the old one with only necessary changes — small “# route changes,” low reopt time.

## 8\. Before / After Metrics (definitions)

Snapshot the plan immediately **before** applying an event and immediately **after** re-optimization; diff them.

| Metric | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Total distance | Σ arc distances over all vehicle routes (km) |
| Total delivery time | Σ (last-stop ETA − vehicle start) across vehicles, or makespan |
| Late deliveries | count of stops with `eta > window_end` |
| Route changes | stops whose `(vehicle, seq)` differs from the previous plan |
| Vehicle utilization | avg `current+planned load / capacity` across active vehicles (%) |
| Re-optimization time | wall-clock ms of the `reoptimize()` call |

Show as two columns with green/red delta badges; utilization also as a bar per vehicle.

## 10\. Demo Runbook (the story to tell)

1. Load scenario — depot, 4 vehicles, ~15 orders with mixed windows/priorities. Show the map.
2. Optimize — press Optimize; routes appear. Note the baseline metrics.
3. Press Play — trucks start moving; let 2 stops on one vehicle complete.
4. Trigger the money shot — vehicle breakdown after stop 2. Show that stops 1–2 stay done, and only stops 3+ get redistributed to other vehicles. Point at “# route changes” (small) and “reopt time” (< 5s).
5. Priority order appears — mid-drive, inject a Critical order; watch it get inserted and a low-priority order possibly dropped.
6. Traffic spike — slow a region; a route resequences to avoid it.
7. Before/After — narrate the deltas: fewer late deliveries, stable committed work, fast re-opt.

Key talking point: *“We never re-plan from scratch — completed and in-progress deliveries are frozen, and the solver warm-starts from the current plan, so it reacts in seconds and doesn’t yank drivers off routes they’ve already committed to.”*

 *

## 11\. Risks & Fallbacks

*   **OSRM/ORS rate limits or offline** → haversine×1.3 matrix fallback (already in plan); cache aggressively.
*   **Re-opt too slow on big instances** → shrink time limit, only rebuild the affected vehicles’ sub-problem, cap node count for demo.
*   **Infeasible after event** → disjunction drops lowest-priority orders instead of erroring; surface dropped orders in the UI.
*   **Socket churn** → throttle position broadcasts (e.g. 2–4 Hz); send plan diffs, not full plans.
*   **Scope creep** → SQLite persistence, auth, multi-depot are *optional* stretch goals; skip until the core loop demos cleanly.

 *

## 12\. Definition of Done

- [ ] Map shows live vehicles, routes, priority-colored orders.
- [ ] Orders and vehicles are fully manageable with all required fields.
- [ ] Initial optimizer respects capacity, windows, hours, travel, priority.
- [ ] All 7 events trigger correct, partial re-optimization.
- [ ] Completed/in-progress deliveries provably never change.
- [ ] Before/After shows all six metrics with real deltas.
- [ ] Demo runbook completes end-to-end.
